newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH FIRMS' CREDIT DEMAND SEEN RISING - SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH FIRMS' CREDIT DEMAND SEEN RISING - SURVEY.

text.p: Finnish companies' demand for new credit appears to be rising, but firms are still cautious about actually signing up for new loans, the Ministry of Trade and Industry said in a statement on Tuesday.

"Two thirds of small and medium-sized companies, for example, are not planning to raise any new financing during the next half year," the ministry said referring to a financing survey made jointly with the Bank of Finland and the Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers.

An increasing share of new financing was being granted by banks, while big companies had issued more bonds. The number of companies planning to raise new bank credits within the next six months had also increased, the ministry said.
"In the future, demand for bank credits seems to be increasing particularly in the service sector," it said.
Of big industrial companies, 61 percent had raised new credits during the past six months, most of which were large foreign credits for replacing old credits at more unfavourable terms, it said.
Small companies were investing their surplus cash mainly in bank deposits, while big companies favoured money market instruments.
The financial position of companies and problems with collateral had eased significantly compared to what the situation was two or three years ago, the ministry said.
